analysis_notes.gap_analysis_detail: Torah #231 is a two-paragraph teaching composed entirely of eitza (causal/instrumental) language. The source text was read in full. No instance of 'בְּחִינַת', 'נקרא', or equivalent bechina language was found. The concepts present in the text — צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם (host of heaven), כֹּחוֹת הַגַּלְגַּלִּים (forces of the celestial spheres), סַמִּים וַעֲשָׂבִים (herbs and remedies), רְפוּאָה (healing), תְּפִלָּה (prayer), חֲתִיכַת לֶחֶם (a piece of bread) — are all connected by 'עַל יְדֵי' (through), 'מְקַבְּלִים' (receive), and 'עַל כֵּן' (therefore). These are unambiguously eitza relationships (one produces/enables another), not bechina relationships (same essential nature). Accordingly there are no missing bechina nodes to flag, no orphaned dataset nodes, and no gap additions to propose. The text itself references 'עַיֵּן עִנְיָן זֶה בַּאֲרִיכוּת בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא בְּסִימָן א' (see this topic at length in LM Tinyana Siman 1), indicating that the full bechina-based elaboration of these concepts belongs to LM2:1, not to this brief summary.
